name: Atlanta United FC
notes: US clubs publish no accounts: revenue ($105m) and operating income ($10m, EBITDA) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 MLS season from the Feb 2026 MLS list, cited through its Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com/sites answers scripts with a bot challenge; Forbes' May 2026 soccer list team page repeats the $1B value and $105M revenue but labels the season 2024-2025 and shows Debt/Value 0%. Capacity is the stadium operator's figure for the venue (72,000 seats scalable to 83,000); the smaller configuration Atlanta United normally uses for MLS matches is not stated on a page read here (Forbes lists 75,000). The shirt-sponsor source is the club's record of the 2016 American Family Insurance deal; a Feb 2025 fan-site report on The Connector kit (Scarves and Spikes, in sources) says AFI is the main jersey sponsor for a ninth straight year, and AFI is still in the club's 2026 partner footer. AMBSE CEO Rich McKay sits above Culebro. In August 2026 CNBC (via Yahoo/Falcons Wire) reported Arctos agreeing to buy 10% of the Atlanta Falcons at a $10.6bn valuation; the reports concern the NFL team and do not mention Atlanta United, so no institutional owner is recorded here. LLC registry number and social follower counts not found.

owners.evidence: with Arthur M. Blank as the Club owner
owners.name: Arthur M. Blank

ownership_summary: Arthur M. Blank has owned Atlanta United since Major League Soccer awarded him the Atlanta expansion team on 16 April 2014; the club (Atlanta United Football Club, LLC) is run by his AMB Sports and Entertainment (AMBSE), which also runs the NFL's Atlanta Falcons. No minority or institutional investor in the club is reported, and Forbes' 2026 MLS valuation list names Blank as the key owner.
